what: highlight "the greatest philosopher in the known world"
said: His name was Timothy Dexter. He called himself Lord Timothy Dexter. And he believed he was the greatest philosopher in the known world.

what: highlight "He became wealthy through marriage and a series of improbably successful investments"
said: He could barely read or write. He became rich through marriage and a string of investments so unlikely they sound made up.

what: highlight "He was from a poor family of Irish and English descent"
said: Timothy Dexter was born in January seventeen forty-seven, in Malden, Massachusetts. His family was poor.

what: highlight "dropped out of school to work as a farm laborer at the age of 8"
said: He dropped out of school at age eight to work as a farm laborer. At sixteen, he became an apprentice to a tanner, someone who turns animal skins into leather.

what: highlight "He married 32-year-old Elizabeth Frothingham, a rich widow"
said: In seventeen sixty-nine, he moved to the port town of Newburyport. There, he married a wealthy widow named Elizabeth Frothingham.

what: highlight "In March 1776, he was appointed"
said: Even before he was rich, he loved titles. In March seventeen seventy-six, the town appointed him Informer of Deer. His job was to tell people when deer were nearby, and enforce the hunting rules.

what: highlight "despite the fact that there were no deer in the Newburyport area"
said: There was one small problem. There were no deer in the Newburyport area. He was proud of the job anyway, and was re-elected every year until seventeen eighty-eight.

what: highlight "The Continental Congress also issued paper money during the revolution"
said: During the American Revolution, the new Continental Congress paid for the war by printing paper money. It was called continental currency.

what: highlight "led to rampant inflation and the phrase"
said: They printed so much of it that its value collapsed. People started using a new phrase for anything useless. Not worth a continental.

what: highlight "prompting the United States to adopt a bimetallic standard of gold and silver under the Coinage Act of 1792"
said: That disaster taught the young country a lesson. A few years later, in seventeen ninety-two, the United States tied its new dollar to gold and silver, to make sure people could trust it.

what: highlight "he purchased large amounts of depreciated Continental currency that were worthless at the time"
said: Near the end of the war, Dexter did something everyone thought was crazy. He bought huge amounts of this nearly worthless money.

what: highlight "Massachusetts paid its own notes at par"
said: Then the war ended. The national government paid its notes back at only one percent of face value. But Massachusetts paid its own notes back at full value.

what: highlight "This advice was a deliberate ploy by rivals to bankrupt him."
said: They told him to ship bed warmers to the West Indies. A bed warmer is a metal pan you fill with hot coals to warm your bed on cold New England nights.

what: highlight "His ship's captain sold them as ladles to the local molasses industry and made a handsome profit."
said: But his ship's captain had an idea. He sold the pans as ladles to the local molasses industry, which needed big metal scoops. They made a handsome profit.

what: highlight "Dexter sent wool mittens to the same place, where Asian merchants bought them for export to Siberia"
said: Next, he sent wool mittens to the same tropical islands. Another terrible idea. But merchants bought them to resell in Siberia, one of the coldest places on Earth.

what: highlight "Dexter supposedly took the joke literally and sent shipments of coal to Newcastle"
said: Think about how unlikely that is. It is like someone telling you to sell sand in the desert, and you show up the one week a sandstorm wiped out the local supply.

what: highlight "he did so during a Newcastle miners' strike, and his cargo was sold at a premium"
said: His coal arrived during a miners' strike. The mines were shut, and the town desperately needed coal. His cargo sold at a premium. A premium means above the normal price.

what: highlight "His ships arrived there in time to sell the gloves to Portuguese boats on their way to China."
said: The list goes on. Practical jokers told him to ship gloves to the South Sea Islands. His ships arrived just in time to sell them to Portuguese sailors heading to China.

what: highlight "the Caribbean welcomed a solution to rat infestation"
said: He sent Bibles to the East Indies, where missionaries needed them. He sent stray cats to Caribbean islands, which had a rat problem. Both made money.

what: highlight "He also hoarded whalebones by mistake, but ended up selling them profitably as corset stays"
said: He even piled up whalebones by mistake, and then sold them at a profit for corsets, the stiff undergarments that were fashionable at the time.

what: highlight "he understood the value of cornering the market on goods that others did not see as valuable"
said: A researcher named Stephen Gencarella argues that Dexter may have understood something real. Buying up goods nobody else wanted, and acting the fool on purpose.

what: highlight "the statistician Abraham Wald described methods of estimating the vulnerability of various parts of an aircraft"
said: In World War Two, a statistician named Abraham Wald studied planes that came back from battle covered in bullet holes. The military wanted to add armor where the holes were.

what: highlight "would overlook the question of where non-surviving planes were fatally hit"
said: Wald pointed out the problem. Those were the planes that survived. The planes hit in other places never came back to be counted.

what: highlight "Survivorship bias may lead to overly optimistic beliefs because multiple failures are overlooked"
said: Survivorship bias can make us far too optimistic, because all the failures are quietly left out of the story.

what: highlight "a garden of 40 wooden statues of famous men"
said: So he built a mansion and decorated it his own way. Towers, a golden eagle on top, and a garden of forty wooden statues of famous men. George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Napoleon. And himself.

what: highlight "about 3,000 people attended Dexter's mock wake"
said: He paid children a quarter to call him Lord Chester. One time, he faked his own death to see how people would react. About three thousand people came to his fake funeral.

what: highlight "the woman frequenting the building was simply her ghost"
said: He also liked to tell visitors that his wife, who was very much alive, had died, and that the woman they saw in the house was only her ghost.

what: highlight "The book contains 8,847 words and 33,864 letters, but without any punctuation"
said: At age fifty, he wrote a book called A Pickle for the Knowing Ones. It has more than eight thousand words, and not a single punctuation mark.

what: highlight "Ime the first Lord in the younited States of A mercary"
said: One famous line begins, I am the first Lord in the United States of America. Except he spelled almost every word in his own creative way.

what: highlight "by adding an extra page of 11 lines of punctuation marks"
said: People complained. So in the second edition, he added a whole page of punctuation marks at the end, and told readers to sprinkle them wherever they liked. Pepper and salt it as they please.

what: highlight "it became popular and was reprinted eight times"
said: And the strangest part? The book became popular, and was reprinted eight times.

what: highlight "his intellectual endowments not ... of the most exalted stamp"
said: Not everyone was impressed. Even his obituary politely said that his intellectual gifts were not of the most exalted kind.

what: highlight "Lord Dexter is a man of fame"
said: So he hired a local fish seller and amateur poet to write verses praising him. One line called him more precious far than gold that is pure.

what: highlight "auctioned off on May 12, 1807"
said: A year after he died, his furniture, the golden balls on his house, and many of his statues were sold off at auction.

what: highlight "valued his estate at $35,027.39"
said: A year after he died, his furniture, the golden balls on his house, and many of his statues were sold off at auction.

what: highlight "nearly 30 times the $17.25 valuation at the beginning of the month"
said: In January twenty twenty-one, people on Reddit piled into GameStop, a struggling video game store. At its peak, the stock was nearly thirty times higher than at the start of the month.

what: highlight "Robinhood halted purchases of GameStop"
said: It got so wild that some trading apps, including Robinhood, stopped people from buying the stock for a while.

what: highlight "79% of fund managers underperformed the S&P in 2021"
said: Even professionals struggle to beat the market over time. In twenty twenty-one, seventy-nine percent of fund managers did worse than the simple S and P five hundred index.

what: highlight "The Great September Gale of 1815"
said: Timothy Dexter's house still stands in Newburyport, Massachusetts. A big storm in eighteen fifteen knocked down most of his wooden statues. But his legend is still standing.
